title: Noetherian koszul procomparison
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in A$ a finite list, and $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$. Let $Q_m(A)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[A\xrightarrow{a_j^m}A]$ in degrees $[-r,0]$, with transition multiplication by $a_j$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$ in each factor. Here tensor products are total tensor products of ordinary $A$-module complexes: degree $q$ is the direct sum over tuples of degrees with sum $q$, and the differential has the usual sign $(-1)^{p_1+\cdots+p_{j-1}}$ on the differential of factor $j$. Equivalently, this is [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] on the one-object site with only the identity covering and constant ring $A$. The degree-zero quotient maps define a strict morphism of towers $\epsilon_m:Q_m(A)\to A/I^m[0]$ of complexes of $A$-modules. In $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the tower of its mapping cones is pro-zero: for every $m\geq1$ there is $k\geq m$ such that the induced transition $\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_k)\to\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_m)$ is the zero morphism in $D(A)$. Mapping cones and their transition maps are those of the strict commutative squares of complexes.

source.place: Tag 0921 (lemma-sequence-Koszul-complexes), with the cofinal ideals (a_1^m,...,a_r^m) and I^m in the proof of Tag 0922 (proposition-noetherian-naive-completion-is-completion); zero cone transitions follow from Tags 0G3B/0G3C in derived.tex.

proof.text: Put $J_m=(a_1^m,\ldots,a_r^m)$ and $C_m=\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_m)$. Each $a_j^m$ lies in $I^m$, so the quotient $A\to A/I^m$ kills the differential into $Q_m^0=A$ and defines the claimed augmentation. For $k\geq m$, its square commutes strictly: the map $Q_k^0\to Q_m^0$ is the identity, and both paths send $x\in A$ to its class modulo $I^m$. On the summand indexed by $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$, in degree $-|S|$, the transition $Q_k\to Q_m$ is multiplication by $\prod_{j\in S}a_j^{k-m}$. The total-tensor sign rule gives the differential $d(e_S)=\sum_{j\in S}(-1)^{\operatorname{pos}(j,S)-1}a_j^m e_{S\setminus\{j\}}$, where $S$ is increasingly ordered. The differential and transition formulas commute term by term since $a_j^m a_j^{k-m}=a_j^k$. For $r=0$, $I=0$ and $Q_m=A[0]$, so $\epsilon_m$ is the identity and $C_m$ is acyclic; the conclusion follows directly from localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Hence assume $r\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0BKC (situation-koszul), transition formula after that situation; Tag 0921 (lemma-sequence-Koszul-complexes)

proof.text: For each $j$ let $h_j$ be signed insertion of $j$ into a basis subset: $h_j(e_S)=0$ if $j\in S$, and otherwise $h_j(e_S)=(-1)^{\#\{i\in S:i<j\}}e_{S\cup\{j\}}$. It lowers cohomological degree by one. Expanding the preceding differential, the terms deleting an index different from $j$ cancel in $dh_j+h_jd$, and the term deleting $j$ is $a_j^m e_S$; when $j\in S$ the latter term comes from $h_jd$. Thus $dh_j+h_jd=a_j^m\mathrm{id}$. For a cycle $z$, $a_j^m z=d(h_jz)$, so $J_m Z_m^p\subseteq B_m^p$, where $Z_m^p=\ker(d:Q_m^p\to Q_m^{p+1})$ and $B_m^p=\operatorname{im}(d:Q_m^{p-1}\to Q_m^p)$. This proves the annihilation needed below directly from the finite basis formulas; no regular-sequence hypothesis is used.

Fix $m\geq1$ and $-r\leq p<0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to the ideal $J_m$, the finite free module $M=Q_m^p$ and its submodule $N=Z_m^p$. Its hypotheses hold: $A$ is Noetherian and $Q_m^p$ has the finite subset basis above. Obtain $c\geq0$ with $J_m^{c+1}M\cap N\subseteq J_m N$. Choose $k\geq m+m(c+1)$. Since $S$ is nonempty in degree $p<0$, each diagonal transition coefficient contains some factor $a_j^{k-m}\in J_m^{c+1}$. A cycle of $Q_k$ therefore maps into $J_m^{c+1}M\cap Z_m^p\subseteq J_m Z_m^p\subseteq B_m^p$ by step 2. Consequently $H^p(Q_k)\to H^p(Q_m)$ is zero. Enlarging $k$ preserves this property by composition of transitions. Taking a maximum over the finitely many $p=-r,\ldots,-1$ gives a single $k$ killing all negative Koszul cohomology transitions to level $m$.

Compute cohomology of the strict cone from its defining differential in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its terms are $C_m^0=A/I^m$, $C_m^{-1}=Q_m^0=A$, and $C_m^q=Q_m^{q+1}$ for $q\leq-2$; the differential $C_m^{-1}\to C_m^0$ is the quotient, and the lower differentials are $-d_{Q_m}$. Thus $H^0(C_m)=0$, $H^{-1}(C_m)=I^m/J_m$, and $H^q(C_m)=H^{q+1}(Q_m)$ for $q\leq-2$. These identifications describe the transitions too: the cone map is the quotient in degree zero, the identity on $A$ in degree $-1$, and the map $Q_k^{q+1}\to Q_m^{q+1}$ in degrees $q\leq-2$. In particular, the transition $I^k/J_k\to I^m/J_m$ sends the class of $x$ to the class of the same $x$. For $s=r(m-1)+1$, every degree-$s$ monomial in the generators has some generator with exponent at least $m$, so $I^s\subseteq J_m$. Therefore any $k\geq\max(m,s)$ kills this degree-$-1$ transition. Step 3 kills all degrees $q\leq-2$ eventually. The cones have terms only in $[-r-1,0]$, independently of $m$.

source.place: Tag 0922 (proposition-noetherian-naive-completion-is-completion), cofinal-power paragraph, expanded via the cone differential of derived.tex (definition-cone)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-tower-pro-zero] to $X_m=C_m$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$. The strict commuting squares of step 1 give actual cone chain maps; their composites and identities are the cone maps of the composite squares, so they are a tower in the derived category. Its cohomology is uniformly supported in $[-r-1,0]$ by step 4. For every degree and every target level, steps 3 and 4 provide a later level killing the induced cohomology map (outside the range it is already zero). All hypotheses of the cited bounded-tower lemma hold, so for each $m$ some $k\geq m$ makes the very same transition $C_k\to C_m$ zero in $D(A)$, as required. This final upgrade is essential: one cohomologically zero morphism alone need not be zero in the derived category.
